questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the challenges / they ultimate achieved / their goal of launching / their startup.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of the word '**ultimate'.**
 
• **'achieved'** is a **verb**, and hence, the word that must modify it should be an **adverb**.
 
• 'ultimate' is an **adjective**, and hence, it must be replaced by an **adverb**.
 
• "**ultimately**" (adverb) must replace 'ultimate' to make the sentence grammatically correct. 

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Despite the challenges, they **ultimately **achieved their goal of launching their startup."*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word(s) in the given sentence.

Monik said that it is mandatory that __each student pay__ his/her tuition fees every month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **each student pays**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**each student**," which is **singular **and requires a **singular verb**.
 
• The correct singular form of the verb "pay" in the present tense is "**pays**."
 
• The construction "**it is mandatory that**" indicates a general rule or obligation, hence the present tense verb "**pays**" is appropriate.
 
• Other options do not fit the grammatical context:
 
 
• **Paids**: Incorrect because "paids" is not a valid form of the verb "pay."
 
• **Paid**: Incorrect as it is the past tense form and does not fit the present obligation context.
 
• **Students pay**: Incorrect because "each student" is singular, not plural.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Monik said that it is mandatory that **each student pays**__ his/her tuition fees every month."*

questions.solution:

• The word **"gave up"** typically means to stop doing something; to surrender or relinquish. (छोड़ देना)

 
 
• **Example: **He gave up smoking after his doctor advised him to quit for his health.
 
 
 
• **"gave away"** means to distribute something for free; to hand something out. (बांटना)
 
 
• **Example: **The charity organization gave away blankets to the homeless during the winter.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct substitution for 'gave up' in the given sentence is 'gave away'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. 'gave away'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The thieves had no alternative/ but to acquiesce with/ the orders of/ the police.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary issue in the sentence lies in the incorrect use of the preposition "**with**" after the verb "**acquiesce**."
 
• The correct preposition that follows "**acquiesce**" is "**to**," not "with."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**acquiesce to** the orders of," which means to agree or comply passively.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

**Correct Sentence:** *The thieves had no alternative but to **acquiesce to** the orders of the police.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The head coach declared that the player **__who will score the most points__** in the game will clinch the trophy this year

options.text: who were score the maximum points
who have score the maximum points

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is based on the **first conditional** structure, which is used to talk about real and possible situations in the future.
 
• The rule for the first conditional is: **If + present simple, will + base verb**.
 
• In this context, the clause "**who scores the maximum points**" correctly uses the **present simple** tense, aligning with the future result "**will clinch the trophy**."

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The head coach declared that the player who **scores the maximum points** in the game will clinch the trophy this year.*

• Other options do not fit the context:
 
 
• **The**: Definite article, does not indicate possession.
 
• **It's**: Contraction for "it is" or "it has," not showing possession.
 
• **There**: Refers to a place or position, irrelevant in this context.
